bug_semantics: Before the fix, both PATCH /boards/{boardID}/blocks/{blockID} and the batch PATCH /boards/{boardID}/blocks endpoint treated a comment as an ordinary board block. An authenticated user with board-wide PermissionManageBoardCards (the editor capability) could name a comment created by another member and alter its title/fields: the handlers checked board access/association but did not compare block.CreatedBy with the session user or require the elevated PermissionDeleteOthersComments capability. The single endpoint then called PatchBlockAndNotify and the batch endpoint called PatchBlocksAndNotify, so the unauthorized patch reached persistent storage. The fix loads each target and, for TypeComment with CreatedBy != userID, rejects the request unless PermissionDeleteOthersComments is present; it also preserves the original creator/create time in the insert/history path.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable BIC is PR #877 member 7c1d63a9d9ee6a5f82655f780196d96f35cdd12e ('Adding support for patch blocks'), not the mainline squash c734cfb8d16b1a4a20e3fb03b3afdf052fa53fce. That member first registered a session-authenticated PATCH-by-block-ID route and implemented handlePatchBlock as getContainer -> decode arbitrary BlockPatch -> App.PatchBlock, without loading the target for a comment-owner authorization decision. Its parent already supported the 'comment' block type and rendered comments, but had no PATCH route or handlePatchBlock. Later 3450eb6d4ffda75d303f53795b3d7c38cecd2330 added the batch variant; aa540e73ce669a1acd491a5edd7d55199ef1b87c converted the guard to board-wide PermissionManageBoardCards while retaining the missing object-owner check; c1f2ae63165dfc5a162b6d364c3f1644e5114a1c only moved the handler to server/api/blocks.go. The October 2025 deletion fix 80c4012a52f3d59ef38ddde90f12cb761b33caa6 protected deletion of others' comments but left modification exposed.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. GitHub's commit object for 7c1d63a9d9ee6a5f82655f780196d96f35cdd12e records author and committer Jesús Espino <jespinog@gmail.com>, message exactly 'Adding support for patch blocks', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.

AI check: the BIC API commit object gives human author/committer and the one-line message quoted in ai_marker with no trailers.
reasoning: The issue is an object-level authorization failure, not a generic permission failure: editor status legitimately allows card/block management, but a comment's creator establishes an additional ownership boundary. The earliest surviving code path that bypassed that boundary is the direct PR member that created PATCH-by-ID; the mainline commit is provably a squash of that PR and is therefore rejected as the BIC. Its immediate parent contains comments but no PATCH handler, so absence is direct rather than inferred. Later permission work, batch support, file movement, and the deletion-only authorization change preserve or broaden the original flaw but do not precede it. The closing commit guards both mutation endpoints before applying patches and is tied to both repository tags and Mattermost release branches. Because the only permissible AI evidence source—the BIC commit object—contains a human identity and no AI/bot trailer or marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
